newsitem.title: USA: Stocks suffer another battering; Dow drops 93 points.
newsitem.headline: Stocks suffer another battering; Dow drops 93 points.

text.p: The stock market was pounded by a broad wave of selling Thursday as Wall Street grew nervous about the upturn in long-term interest rates and a weakening dollar.
The Dow Jones industrial average ended down 92.75 points, or 1.32 percent, at 6,927.38, one day after losing more than 47 points.
On Tuesday, it set a record high of 7,067.46 after closing for the first time above the 7,000 level last Thursday.
In the broader market, declining issues beat advances 1,679 to 840 on active volume of 490 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

"We've had day after day of stocks going up," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "Now it appears some money managers are taking some chips off the table in the best-performing groups," he said.
Technology and financial stocks met with some of the stiffest selling, with the latter under extra pressure from an ongoing bond market decline.
Tech stocks turned in a particularly choppy performance, even when compared with an overall market that displays ever-increasing volatility by the day.

"We're in a stage of the market where volatility is going to remain quite high," said Charlie Crane, director of research at Spears Benzak Salomon & Farrell. "There is a broad variety of opinions being expressed by market observers and at any given moment one camp will gain an upper hand.
"In technology, there may be the greatest degree of controversy about the profit outlook," he said.
International Business Machines Corp. fell 2-5/8 to 141, Intel Corp. shed four to 149-7/8 and Microsoft Corp. dipped 2-1/4 to 95-1/4.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond nearly a full point, raising its yield to 6.65 percent from 6.58 percent Wednesday. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.
The dollar, which has been flying higher for the past year, fell on signs of economic strength in Europe and more verbal attempts by German central bank officials to tame its recent strength.
It closed at 122.45 Japanese yen, more than two yen below Wednesday's 124.55 close. Against the German mark, the dollar fell to 1.6835 from 1.6980.
The dollar was hit by another call from Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer for an end to its rise against the mark.

Shares in gold and silver mining companies bucked the trend, buoyed by a sharp rise in precious metals prices as the sector benefited from uncertainty about the near-term direction of the stock market.
Newmont Mining Corp. gained 1-7/8 to 46-1/8, Barrick Gold Corp. rose 3/4 to 26-7/8 and Coeur D'Alene Mines Corp. jumped 1-1/4 to 18-1/8.
On New York's Commodity Exchange, the pace-setting April gold contract closed up $5.00 at $352.60 per ounce.
The dollar's strength has been an important factor in the stock market's rally. It has drawn considerable investment to U.S. financial markets from outside the country.

With the stock market still near all-time high levels, the possibility that ebbing dollar strength and slower mutual fund contributions, which dip seasonally after January, could spell more near-term trouble for stocks, analysts said.
"The belief is that perhaps stocks may be entering into a period of correction for a while," said Harry Laubscher, an analyst at Tucker Anthony. "The market has been looking kind of 'toppy' lately."
Shares of oil companies dropped as oil prices fell to six-month lows. Mobil Corp. lost two points to 128-1/4 and Chevron Corp. fell 1-5/8 to 65-5/8.
Crude oil for delivery in March closed 81 cents lower at $21.98 a barrel on the New York Mercantile Exchange.
Cyrix Corp. jumped 3-7/8 to 29-3/8 on news it would supply Compaq Computer Corp. with a microprocessor for use in a new low-cost computer line. But Compaq fell 2-3/4 to 82-5/8.
The Nasdaq Composite index fell 18.18 points to 1,347.40.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks fell 9.69 to 802.80. The American Stock Exchange index slipped 1.72 to 597.43.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks fell 4.48 to 421.09. The average share was down 46 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,687.246, down 85.862, or 1.10 percent.
